explanation: The Nile corresponds to Mesopotamia: the Nile is the source of the Egyptian civilization, while Mesopotamia is the source of the ancient Sumerian civilization. Both are the geographical foundations of their respective civilizations.

The Pyramid corresponds to the Code of Hammurabi: the Pyramid is the representative architecture of the Egyptian civilization, while the Code of Hammurabi is the representative legal code of the ancient Sumerian civilization. Both are important symbols of their respective civilizations.

Hieroglyphs correspond to cuneiform: Hieroglyphs are the writing system of the Egyptian civilization, while cuneiform is the writing system of the ancient Sumerian civilization. Both are the ways of expression of their respective civilizations.

Pharaoh corresponds to the Persian Empire: Pharaoh is the highest ruler of the Egyptian civilization, while the Persian Empire is an important empire of the ancient Sumerian civilization. Both are the political representatives of their respective civilizations.

background.source: Egypt, officially known as the Arab Republic of Egypt, is a transcontinental country located in the northeast corner of Africa and the southwest corner of Asia, connected via the Sinai Peninsula. It has a rich heritage dating back to the 6th–4th millennium BCE, and is considered a cradle of civilisation. Egypt is renowned for its iconic monuments such as the Pyramids of Giza and Sphinx, as well as its vast collection of hieroglyphs representing the history and language of the region. With over 100 million inhabitants, it is the 14th-most populated country on the planet, and is considered a regional power in North Africa, the Middle East and the Muslim world, with a diversified economy ranking 33rd-largest in the world by nominal GDP. Egypt's long and rich cultural heritage is an integral part of its national identity, highlighting its unique transcontinental location being simultaneously Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and North African.
background.target: Ancient Western Asia, also known as the ancient Near East, was the birthplace of some of the earliest civilizations on earth. This region, encompassing modern-day countries such as Iraq, Iran, and Syria, was home to cultures that developed many of the core institutions and technologies we take for granted today. From the first dense urban settlements and centralized governments to the development of the first writing system (using cuneiform) and the first alphabet (known as the abjad), the ancient Near East created a rich legacy that continues to influence our lives today. This was also a time when empires formed, with the powerful Persian Empire rising to control much of the region. One famous legacy from this period was the Code of Hammurabi, which established one of the world's first legal codes. Dive into the history and culture of this fascinating area by exploring the wonders of Mesopotamia and other ancient Near Eastern cultures.
